```{r}
#function that reads scsconda output files and binds them into one tibble
make_df <- function(rel_path_folder="..\\python\\", pattern="mild_vs_control.csv"){
  files_names<- list.files(rel_path_folder) %>% str_subset(pattern) %>% paste0(rel_path_folder,.)
  files_names%>%
  #create alist of tibbles of the scConda results
  map(read_csv) %>%
  #add a column to each tibble with the comparison of the table
  map2(files_names,~mutate(.x, comparison=.y)) %>% 
  #merge all into one dataframe
  map_df(~bind_rows(.x))
  
}

#pipe function that summaries the aggregated scCoda tibble into how many of the comparisons were up or downregulated
sum_up_down <- . %>% 
  clean_names() %>%
  select(covariate,cell_type,final_parameter) %>% 
  mutate(up=ifelse(final_parameter>0,1,0),
         down=ifelse(final_parameter<0,1,0)) %>% 
  group_by(cell_type) %>% 
  summarise(sum_up=sum(up), sum_down=sum(down)) %>% 
  mutate(sum_down=-sum_down) %>% 
  #long format for plotting
  pivot_longer(cols = sum_up:sum_down,names_to = "up_down") %>%
  #actually this is not needed as no there are no cellt ypes that have both  negative and positive entries
  #however 0 values are duplicated and will over plot the other values, removed later
  #filter(up_down!="sum_up" | value!=0) %>% 
  #factor for non-continous scale for plotting
  mutate(majority=ifelse(abs(value)>6,"majority","minority"),value= factor(value,levels =c(-13:13) ))
```
